# Tasks

[reports/](reports/) (`<id>.md`: what was done, what was found, what changed). Status: `todo`, `doing`, `done`,
`blocked`.

## M5: input path and completion (revised 2026-10-18 after T5.01)

Findings that changed the plan: NVENC on Ada reads only its own input layout (64x16 tiles of 16x4 sub-blocks, T2.05d);
`input_bl_mode` is ignored, and neither the classic GOB layout (what the copy engine writes) nor pitch-linear input
decodes correctly, with any block_height. A copy-engine pass from the IOSurface therefore can't feed NVENC directly; a
GPU path needs a compute pass (Metal, in the plugin's RM client) and cross-client memory sharing. The CPU path comes
first.

| ID | Task | Done when | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| T5.01 | Measure the per-frame cost: CPU tiling vs engine (`tools/tilebench`) | numbers for 1080p and 4K | done |
| T5.02 | Fast tiling: SSE/AVX2 tile writes (64x16 tiles), optionally split over threads | 4K tiling ≤ 1 ms | done |
| T5.03 | Asynchronous encode: submit frame n and return; emit when the engine is done (output thread), so tiling of n+1 overlaps encoding of n | throughput limited by the engine, not CPU + engine | done |
| T5.04 | Event-driven completion: RM event / semaphore wake instead of spinning | encode thread sleeps while the engine works | done |
| T5.05 | Measure Parsec 4K: time per frame inside our encoder (needs a parsecd restart: user) | well under ~9 ms | done (Parsec L 4.7-4.8 ms, was ~10.5-12 ms with nullmoth's) |
| T5.06 | GPU swizzle (later): Metal compute pass from the IOSurface into NVENC's layout, memory shared with our RM client | no CPU pass over the frame | measured, not adopted (GPU 1.9 ms vs CPU 0.87 ms at 4K: surfaces are in system RAM) |
| T5.07 | M5 notes, commit | committed | done |

| T7.09 | NVIDIA's lookahead and two-pass modes (third Linux-driver trace: `vla`, `vtaq`, `vmp`) | adopted where they measurably help | done 2026-10-20: **(1) two-pass** (`EncConfig.two_pass`, encodeN `TWOPASS=1`, `NVENCVT_TWOPASS=1`): pass 1 = the picture's setup with `two_pass_rc` 1, NVIDIA's cheaper MD block (`hevc_mp1_md`), no transform skip / quantizer cost vectors / SAO, control `RCSTAT_WRITE`, scratch bitstream / status / history / reconstruction / MV buffers; it writes `nvenc_rc_pic_stat_s` + row statistics at the start of the RC data; pass 2 = `two_pass_rc` 2, `RCSTAT_READ`, ME predictor sources + search shapes from NVIDIA's pass 2 (`hevc_mp2_me`: pass 1's vectors as co-located hints). HEVC two passes for I / P only (B in one pass: same quality, 6.0 instead of 7.6 ms per 1080p frame); H.264 for every picture (one-pass B among two-pass anchors undershot by 25 %). Over 900 frames at equal rate: -0.25..+0.65 VMAF for 2x (H.264) / +7 % (HEVC) engine time, so off by default; on 5-second clips +1-2.6, but that came from the next point. **(2) RC initial state**: nvenc_drv.h says the driver initializes the RC process buffer (`NVENC_RC_INIT_COMPLEXITY`); ours was zero, so the model priced bits at nothing and the first IDR took ~37 frames' budget (4.6 Mbit at QP 21 for 120 kbit frames). Now `Wpbi` / `Whist` 16 / 6 / 38 (NVIDIA's untouched values at 1080p: 15-19 / 5-6 / 35-41), `np` / `nb` from the GOP, CPB half full: +0.6-1.0 VMAF at equal rate over 900 frames (H.264 / HEVC, crowd_run / park_joy, `docs/bench/2026-10-20-rc-matrix.txt`), CBR and VBR on target (7.21 for 7.2 instead of 7.44; VT 20 s at 15 Mbit/s: 15.07). **(3) `Np`** = (gop + B - 1) / (B + 1) as the header defines it (NVIDIA's P-only 249 = the same formula); with B pictures GOP - 1 made two-pass start far too high. **(4) VBR fixed**: T7.08 had put NVIDIA's CBR fields (`Ravg` 0) on every mode, so VBR ran at its maximum (14.7 for 7.2 / 14.4); now CBR only. **(5) Lookahead**: the driver scales each frame 4x (CUDA) and encodes it as an H.264 P picture at QP 40 (`src/la.c` does the same, 0.22 ms per 1080p frame; `h264_la_*` templates); its only per-picture effect on the encode setup is `ab_beta` / `prev_act`, which this engine ignores (bit-identical output for any value); NVIDIA's lookahead output still differs from plain CBR, most likely through the RC state the driver writes. Scene-cut IDRs from the lookahead ratio (cuts 1.6-2.2 vs 0.7-0.85) lowered VMAF (B mode -2.9 / -6.5 with a cut every second): not adopted (encodeN `LOOKAHEAD=1 SCENECUT=thr` for research). Temporal AQ = an MB-tree-like map from the lookahead's motion data (not dumped): not reproduced. **(6) encodeN IDR period with B pictures**: counted anchors only and coded the IDR before the B pictures preceding it (invalid after the first period; libnvencvt unaffected): enc_submit_ex callers now place IDRs, encodeN as libnvencvt does |
| T7.10 | HEVC 4K quality: NVIDIA's p7 controls where the full quality mode does not fit the frame period | measurable gain at 4K | done 2026-10-20: `EncConfig.no_cu8` = the p7 ME / MD / quant blocks with the 16x16 minimum CU (`ENC_HEVC_OFF=cu8` for encodeN): park_joy 4K 24 Mbit/s 2 B: fast 72.0 VMAF at 5.4 ms, p7 without 8x8 72.6 at 10.0 ms, p7 with 8x8 72.7 at 21.8 ms. libnvencvt picks it when the full quality mode would exceed 80 % of the frame period and this one (2.5 ms per 1080p frame, scaled) does not (4K up to ~80 fps). VideoToolbox 4K50 20 Mbit/s: crowd_run 72.0 -> 72.6, park_joy 72.0 -> 72.7 (x265 fast 72.1 / 74.1) |

## M8: H.264 hardware decoder (2026-10-19)

Why: nullmoth's driver registers its H.264 decoder (`libnvdec_h264_t2d` on cards before Blackwell) in every process that
uses Metal, and it decodes correctly, but on an RTX 4090 a 4K H.264 stream decodes at **32 fps** (Apple's software
decoder: 30 fps; their HEVC decoder: 175 fps at 4K). 4K60 H.264 playback is not possible, and command-line tools get no
hardware decoder at all (same registration limit as the encoder). Measured with `tools/vtdecode` (x264/x265 test streams,
hardware vs software output compared: bit-exact). Sources: NVIDIA's open-gpu-doc `classes/video/nvdec_drv.h`
(`nvdec_h264_pic_s`, DPB entries, status) and `clc9b0.h` (Ada NVDEC methods), the H.264 standard. Same ground rules as the
encoder (no disassembly or patching of closed binaries). **User, 2026-10-19: headers only for every decoder** - nullmoth's
decoder libraries are not observed at run time either (unlike the encoder's option B); buffer sizes and engine settings
are found by experiment.

| Task | What | Done when | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| T8.00 | Measure the gap: hardware vs software H.264/HEVC decode, correctness and speed (`tools/vtdecode`) | numbers recorded | done: H.264 4K 32 fps (sw 30), 1080p 127 (sw 74); HEVC 4K 175 (sw 84); outputs bit-exact except one HEVC 1080p frame (44 dB) |
| T8.01 | A channel on NVDEC with the NVC9B0 object; host + engine semaphores (`tools/dechello`) | both semaphores land | done: NVDEC0 (engine 0x13; RM exposes no other NVDEC on this RTX 4090), both semaphores in 0.011 ms |
| T8.02 | H.264 bitstream reader: SPS, PPS (scaling lists, fall-back rules), slice header to dec_ref_pic_marking (`src/h264parse.c`), POC types 0-2 | parses x264 streams (High, CABAC, B-frames) and our encoder's | done (`tools/h264parsetest`): x264 default, Baseline (POC type 2), JVT scaling matrices, interlaced MBAFF, strict B-pyramid with 16 refs, 4 slices/picture: 0 parse errors, POC order = container timestamp order for every picture; MMCOs parsed (80 pictures). NVDEC parses slice data itself, so no reference-list construction is needed |
| T8.03 | One IDR picture: picture setup from `nvdec_h264_pic_s`, bitstream buffer, output surface, EXECUTE, status | the decoded luma matches the software decoder (PSNR 99 = identical) | done (`tools/decode1`): bit-exact (luma and chroma) for x264 IDRs at 256x128, 1080p, 2048x1152, 1440p, 3072x1728 and 4K, High/CABAC, Baseline/CAVLC, JVT scaling matrices, 8 slices; 1080p 1.15 ms, 4K 4.5 ms. Found by experiment: (1) `tileFormat` 1 / `gob_height` 0 writes the layout already measured for NVENC's input (64x16-byte tiles, `nvenc_in_offset`); (2) the end of the picture must be signalled in `eos[]` with `explicitEOSPresentFlag` (00 00 01 0b), else the last rows are never written and `error_status` is 0x20 (appending it to the bitstream does not help); (3) pictures wider than 1920 need `H264_SET_MBHIST_BUF_OFFSET` + `mbhist_buffer_size`, else the engine reads address 0 (MMU fault, Xid 31, RC record via `tools/rcerr`). Buffer sizes are still generous guesses (history 8 MB, MB history 8 MB, co-located 512 B/MB) |
| T8.04 | P/B pictures: DPB management (sliding window, MMCO), colocated buffers, reference surfaces | a 300-frame x264 stream with B-frames decodes bit-exact | done (`src/dec.c`, `tools/decodeN`): 11 streams bit-exact, every picture: x264 1080p I/B/P (300 frames), strict B-pyramid with 16 refs and MMCOs, temporal direct, 8 slices, Baseline, JVT matrices, open GOP, 4K, MBAFF, plus OpenH264, Apple's VideoToolbox encoder and our NVENC; 4K 4.65 ms/picture on the engine (215 fps), 1080p ~1.2 ms. Found: a reference must keep its `dpb[]` slot for its whole life (the co-located data names references by slot; moving entries broke temporal direct). Not yet: field pictures (PAFF), frame_num gaps (non-existing frames) |
| T8.05 | Output: decoded surface to NV12 (CVPixelBuffer planes) | 4K at ≥ 120 fps end to end | done: SIMD untile `nvenc_in_untile_plane` (inverse of the encoder's tiler) via `h264dec_read_nv12`, bit-exact; 4K 1.22 ms per picture (720p 0.21 ms), so 4.64 ms engine + 1.22 ms out = ~170 fps sequential (overlapping the copy with the next decode: ~215). NVDEC's display DMA (`enableTFOutput`, every `TilingFormat` 0-4) wrote nothing on Ada |

An ad-hoc-signed decoder bundle in `/Library/Video/Plug-Ins` is passed over (T7.00); the overlay's `--cli-wrappers` (wrappers first in `PATH`) runs plain `ffmpeg` through `nvenc-run` |

## M9-M14: every codec the hardware has (user, 2026-10-19: "we want to add ALL of them")

RTX 4090 (Ada): two NVENC engines (0xc9b7), one NVDEC exposed by RM (0xc9b0), no NVJPG. Picture setups for every codec are
public: `nvdec_drv.h` (H.264, HEVC, VP9, AV1, VP8, MPEG-2, MPEG-4, VC-1) and `nvenc_drv.h` (H.264, HEVC, AV1). The
decoders share M8's pieces: the NVDEC channel and buffers, the output path to CVPixelBuffer (T8.05) and the VideoToolbox
decoder plugin `libnvdecvt` (T8.06), which gains one factory per codec. Order by value: what Macs with NVIDIA cards
lack most first. Each decoder is checked against a software decoder (ffmpeg: libdav1d, libvpx, its own H.264/HEVC/MPEG
decoders) frame by frame, with streams from more than one encoder.

| Milestone | Codec | Tasks (each: done when it decodes/encodes bit-exact or ≥ the stated quality) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| M9 | **AV1 decode** (8/10-bit, `av01`) | T9.01 OBU parser (sequence header, frame header, tile info, reference frame state) · T9.02 one key frame through `nvdec_av1_pic_s` · T9.03 inter frames (reference slots, segmentation, loop filter, CDEF, loop restoration, film grain parameters) · T9.04 VideoToolbox `av01` decoder (av1C) + ffmpeg `-hwaccel videotoolbox` · streams from libaom, SVT-AV1, rav1e | done 2026-10-19 (mesa-nova as reference, see below) |
| M10 | **VP9 decode** (8/10/12-bit, `vp09`) | T10.01 uncompressed + compressed header parser · T10.02 key frame through `nvdec_vp9_pic_s` · T10.03 inter frames, probability contexts (forward updates, backward adaptation counts), reference refresh, scaled references · T10.04 VideoToolbox `vp09` decoder · streams from libvpx | done 2026-10-19 (before M9; see below) |
| M11 | **HEVC decode, ours** (Main, Main 10, Main 12, 4:4:4, `hvc1`) | T11.01 VPS/SPS/PPS/slice header reader (beside `hevchdr.c`) · T11.02 IDR · T11.03 P/B with RPS · T11.04 10/12-bit and 4:4:4 · T11.05 VideoToolbox `hvc1` decoder rated above nullmoth's (theirs: one mismatched frame in the x265 1080p test) | done 2026-10-19 |
| M12 | **AV1 encode** (8/10-bit) | T12.01 OBU writer (sequence and frame headers) · T12.02 one key frame through `nvenc_av1_drv_pic_setup_s` · T12.03 inter frames, references, rate control (CBR/VBR/low latency) · T12.04 10-bit · T12.05 VideoToolbox `av01` encoder | done 2026-10-19 (setup from tracing NVIDIA's Linux driver, see below) |
| M13 | **4:4:4 encode** + encoder probe | T13.01 HEVC Range Extensions 4:4:4 (was T7.04) · T13.02 H.264 High 4:4:4 Predictive · T13.03 probe whether Ada NVENC accepts the VP8 / VP9 application IDs (not in NVIDIA's Ada support matrix; drop if refused) | done 2026-10-20 (VP8 / VP9 encode: not in Ada's NVENC firmware) |
| M14 | **legacy decode** | T14.01 MPEG-2 (`mp2v`) and MPEG-1 · T14.02 MPEG-4 Part 2 (`mp4v`) · T14.03 VC-1 / WMV3 · T14.04 VP8 (`vp08`); VideoToolbox registration only where AVFoundation or ffmpeg can feed the codec | done 2026-10-20 (MPEG-1/2, MPEG-4 Part 2, VC-1, VP8; H.263 not in the engine) |

Not codecs, out of scope: the optical flow accelerator (OFA, 0xc9fa). No JPEG engine on this card.

**Order changed (2026-10-19): VP9 (M10) before AV1 (M9).** With headers only, AV1 is blocked: the engine reads its
symbol probabilities (CDFs) from a buffer whose layout no public header gives (`nvdec_drv.h` has the AV1 picture setup
but no CDF table structure), and NVDEC does not initialise or adapt them itself. VP9's probability tables and counters
are public (`nvdec_vp9EntropyProbs_t`, `nvdec_vp9EntropyCounts_t`), so VP9 goes first; AV1 waits for a layout hypothesis
to test (spec order, padded like VP9's tables).

## M15: GTX 1650 (Turing TU117), 2026-10-20

The RTX 4090 was swapped for an ASUS Phoenix GTX 1650 OC (TU117: NVENC 6.6 = class 0xb4b7, the Volta generation; NVDEC
0xc4b0; host classes c46f / c461). NullMoth 2.4.3 has no encoder for it (its Turing encoders do not register), so ours fill
the gap. User: "start with 1, move to 2 then 3" (1 = trace NVIDIA's Linux driver for the HEVC encode fault, 2 = decoder
gaps, 3 = libnvencvt on TU117 + benchmark against NullMoth's decoders). Report: [reports/T15.md](reports/T15.md).

On NVENC 6.6 the real-time path now uses NVIDIA's own p4 ME / MD / quant controls traced on the card (`h264_nv66_*` in `src/h264enctmpl.h`): encodeN +8.0 / +8.2 / +8.7 VMAF at the same rate (crowd / park 1080p, crowd 4K) and 30 % faster; through VideoToolbox (benchmark rows) +3.2 / +3.7 at 1080p, 4K 13 % faster, latency 4.1 / 15.4 ms (was 4.5 / 17.3). ## M11: HEVC decode

Unlike VP9 and AV1, NVDEC parses HEVC slice data and slice headers itself (`nvdec_hevc_pic_s` is DXVA-like): the driver
gives the SPS / PPS fields, scaling lists, tile sizes, the reference picture set (which DPB entries are references, their
POC distances, long-term flags) and the bit counts of the slice header parts it has parsed already
(`sw_hdr_skip_length`, `num_bits_short_term_ref_pics_in_slice`). Sources: ITU-T H.265, `nvdec_drv.h`, `clc9b0.h`.
Streams: `scripts/make-hevc-streams.sh OUTDIR` (libx265 through ffmpeg) and `scripts/fetch-hevc-vectors.sh OUTDIR` (the
JCT-VC conformance bitstreams from FFmpeg's FATE suite); references from ffmpeg's HEVC decoder.

| Task | What | Done when | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| T11.01 | Parser: NAL units (Annex B, length-prefixed), SPS (profile_tier_level, sub-layer ordering, scaling lists incl. prediction and defaults, short-term RPS incl. inter-RPS prediction (7.4.8), long-term pictures, VUI / HRD, range extension), PPS (tiles, deblocking, scaling lists, range extension), slice segment header (with the bit position and length of the RPS part and of the whole header), POC (8.3.1) | the fields match ffmpeg's `trace_headers` on every test stream, including bit positions | done (`src/hevcparse.c`, `tools/hevcparsetest`, `scripts/hevc-trace-compare.py`, which also compares where the SPS / PPS end, where the RPS starts and ends and where the slice header ends): 26 x265 streams (B-pyramids, open / closed GOP, P only, 8 references, slices, WPP, scaling lists, weighted prediction, lossless, transform skip + AMP, temporal layers, CTB 16 / 32, HRD, RPS in the SPS, 10 / 12-bit, 4:2:2 / 4:4:4, 350x286, 4K) and all 188 conformance bitstreams (base layer of MV-HEVC), 0 differences. Found: a Main-profile PPS may carry garbage in its extension flags (conformance `PS_A`), so the range extension is read for RExt profiles only (as ffmpeg does); `EXT_A_ericsson_3` is unreadable for ffmpeg too (`_4` is fine) |
| T11.02 | One IDR through `nvdec_hevc_pic_s`: SPS / PPS fields, scaling list, tile size, filter, co-located MV buffers | bit-exact against ffmpeg | done (`src/hevcdec.c`, `tools/hevcdecodeN`): the first IDR of an x265 stream was bit-exact on the first try. The slice segments go to the engine with start codes (`sw_start_code_e`), one job per picture; the engine finds and parses them itself. Picture slots = surfaces (`SET_PICTURE_LUMA/CHROMA_OFFSET0..15`, `curr_pic_idx`), co-located MVs at `SET_COLOC_DATA_OFFSET` + slot x `colMvBuffersize` (128 bytes per 16x16 block allocated), filter buffer laid out from `HEVC_DBLK_TOP/LEFT` and `HEVC_SAO_LEFT` with the BSD control, filter above, SAO above and slice edge areas after it (sizes generous), `SET_INTRA_TOP_BUF_OFFSET` and the slice info buffer set as for VP9 |
| T11.03 | P / B pictures: RPS (8.3.2) incl. long-term pictures, initial reference lists (8.3.4), POC, output order and removal (C.5.2), RASL skipping | the x265 streams and the JCT-VC conformance bitstreams bit-exact | done: 27 of 30 x265 streams and 178 of the 186 conformance bitstreams with a reference decode bit-exact on every picture (B-pyramids, 8 references, open GOP, CRA / BLA / RASL / RADL, long-term pictures in the SPS and slice header, list modification, weighted prediction, slices, dependent slices, WPP, tiles, scaling lists, PCM, transform skip, lossless, TMVP, deblocking / SAO variants, conformance window, HRD, filler data, 8 temporal layers, bumping, `no_output_of_prior_pics`, 4K at 2.0 ms / picture). Found: (1) `sw_hdr_skip_length` = the slice header bits after `slice_type` up to the end of the reference picture set (`pic_output_flag`, `colour_plane_id`, `slice_pic_order_cnt_lsb`, the short-term set, the long-term part), which the engine skips because the driver applied them (a sweep over the first P picture: only 17 = 8 + 9 decoded; `OPFLAG_*` needed the `pic_output_flag` bit, also on IDR pictures); anything else answers status 0x5 within 0.04 ms; (2) `num_ref_frames` = NumPicTotalCurr, not every reference: the engine sizes `list_entry_lX` from it (`LTRPSPS_A`, a long-term picture kept for later pictures); `initreflistidxl0/l1` = RefPicListTemp0/1 (the RPS repeated to 16 entries, as slot numbers), `RefDiffPicOrderCnts[slot]` = current POC - reference POC, `longtermflag` bit 15 - slot; (3) scaling lists: DC values, 8 bytes padding, then each list column by column (transposed; the default lists are symmetric, only the `SLIST_*` streams tell); (4) `log2MaxTransformSkipSize` is the full log2 size (2 for 4x4), not "minus2" as its comment says. Output order in `hevcdecodeN` follows C.5.2.2 / C.5.2.3 (reorder, latency and DPB fullness bumping; prior pictures discarded with NoOutputOfPriorPicsFlag). Not decodable: `WPP_D` (pictures 64x240, one 64-pixel CTB per row, with dependent slice segments: the engine answers status 0x5 within 0.04 ms for exactly the pictures whose second / fourth segments are dependent (POC 4, 5, 12), while the same layout with independent segments decodes bit-exact; every CTB starts a row, the corner where the spec's WPP storage / dependent-slice context rules degenerate; extension data stripped from the slice headers did not change it; an engine limit for a layout no real stream has, 2026-10-20), `PICSIZE_A/B` (8440 lines, beyond NVDEC's 8192: refused) |
| T11.04 | 10 / 12-bit, 4:4:4, range extension | bit-exact | done: 10 / 12-bit 4:2:0 and 8 / 10 / 12-bit 4:4:4 bit-exact (x265 incl. 4K 10-bit at 3.2 ms / picture; conformance Main 10 streams, `QMATRIX_A` 4:4:4 with scaling lists, `PERSIST_RPARAM_A`, `SAO_A_RExt`, `WPP_HIGH_TP_444_8BIT`, `IPCM_B_RExt`). Found: (1) `framestride` counts samples, as for VP9 (with bytes, 10-bit rows landed twice as far apart and 4K overran its surface: channel error); (2) 4:4:4 chroma is Cb / Cr interleaved at full width (like NV24) with `framestride[1]` twice the luma stride (with equal strides each 16-row band overwrote half of the previous one). Refused (status 0x5): 4:2:2 (NVIDIA lists it from Blackwell on) and monochrome. Untested: unequal luma / chroma bit depths (`TSUNEQBD_A`, which ffmpeg cannot write as raw video either) |

## M14: legacy decode

NVDEC's MPEG-1/2, MPEG-4 Part 2, VC-1 and VP8 setups are in `nvdec_drv.h`; like H.264 and HEVC the engine parses the
slices itself. Headers only (no tracing, no other implementation); what the headers leave open is found by experiment.
**MPEG-1/2, MPEG-4 and VC-1 have no bit-exact IDCT** (only IEEE 1180 accuracy), so those decoders are checked against
ffmpeg with its most precise IDCT (`-idct faani`, float AAN) and judged against how far ffmpeg's own IDCTs drift apart on
the same stream (`scripts/guest/m2all.sh`).

| Task | What | Done when | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| T14.01 | MPEG-2 / MPEG-1: header parser (sequence, sequence / quant matrix / picture coding extensions, picture header; MPEG-1 defaults), `nvdec_mpeg2_pic_s`, frame and field pictures, I / P / B / D, display order (`src/mpeg2dec.c`, `tools/mpeg2decodeN`); VideoToolbox `mp2v` / `mp1v` in libnvencvt | the ISO 13818-4 conformance streams and ffmpeg-encoded streams decode, every frame within IDCT tolerance | done: **picture slots** (found by experiment): `SET_PICTURE_LUMA/CHROMA_OFFSET0` = the picture decoded (the engine writes slot 0 whatever `SET_PICTURE_INDEX` says), 1 = forward reference, 2 = backward reference; quantiser matrices in **raster** order (zigzag: 34 dB); slices with their start codes plus `SET_SLICE_OFFSETS_BUF_OFFSET`, `eos[]` = sequence end codes; field pictures need only `picture_structure` / `secondfield` (both fields into the same surface); **interlaced sequences: `FrameHeight` rounded up to 32 lines** (720 lines with `progressive_sequence` 0 = 46 macroblock rows; with 720 every picture ended in a 56 ms timeout, status 0x11). ## M12: AV1 encode

NVENC writes only the tile data; the driver writes the OBUs: temporal delimiter, sequence header, and a frame header
carrying what the engine chose (status: `av1_start_QP`, `loop_filter_level`, `cdef_damping_minus_3`), then wraps the
tiles (`tile_stat[]` offsets / sizes) in a frame OBU. Sources: `nvenc_drv.h`, `clc9b7.h`, the AV1 specification, and,
after headers and experiments stalled (see T12.02), **NVIDIA's Linux driver observed at runtime** (the user's decision
2026-10-19): 580.105.08 in the Debian VM that normally owns the RTX 4090, `ffmpeg -c:v av1_nvenc`, recorded with
`trace-linux/nvtrace.so` (LD_PRELOAD on the RM ioctls: escapes, pushed methods, buffers incl. video memory it maps
itself; no disassembly). Traces in `docs/traces/av1-linux/`. NullMoth ships no AV1 encoder; no open-source code drives
NVENC AV1.

| Task | What | Done when | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| T12.01 | OBU writer: sequence header, frame header (key / inter, only the tools NVENC's AV1 encoder uses: 64x64 superblocks, no filter intra / edge filter / inter-intra / masked / joint compound / warped / dual filter / ref frame MVs / screen content / superres / film grain; order hints), frame OBU with tiles | our parser and ffmpeg's `trace_headers` read back what was written | done (`src/av1hdr.c`): key + inter frames at 1080p, 4K with 2 tile columns and 350x286 parse back field for field (0 differences) |
| T12.02 | Key and P frames through `nvenc_av1_drv_pic_setup_s` (`src/enc.c` codec `ENC_AV1`, `encodeN -av1` writes IVF) | dav1d decodes them, PSNR >= 40 dB, no drift | done: 60-frame sequences at 350x286, 640x360, 1280x720, 1080p and 4K decode completely with dav1d at 50 dB (constant quantizer 80 / 100; 1080p 1.4 ms, 4K 4.2 ms per frame). Headers and experiments alone had stalled the engine (findings below); the trace of NVIDIA's driver gave the rest. **What it takes on Ada:** (1) the picture setup is `nvenc_drv.h`'s with **a fourth 32-byte surface config at 0x64** (a copy of the reference picture's), so everything from `seqhdr_data` on sits 32 bytes later than the header says (800 bytes; with the header's layout the engine read the input 16 rows above the picture and stalled); (2) methods: application ID 7, `SET_CONTROL_PARAMS` 0x41905 (codec type 5, force output, tile statistics, app timer, sub-frame mode 2), `pic_control.codec` 7, **no colocated-data methods** (else error 19 before anything else is checked), **one address per picture**: luma and chroma methods of the input and the reconstruction get the same address and the surface configs' plane offsets (units of 256) locate the chroma (reconstruction: luma "bottom" half a plane on, chroma after the 64-row-aligned luma plane, chroma "bottom" half a chroma plane on); P frames add `SET_IN/OUT_MEPRED_DATA` and `SET_IN_REF_PIC0`; (3) **probability tables:** the four default CDF tables in exactly the layout NVDEC reads (our `av1probs.c`, byte-identical to the driver's) at 0x3000 apart with `prob_tables_offset` 0x3000 (the microcode picks one by quantizer) on key frames; P frames read the table the previous frame wrote (`SET_OUT_AV1_PROBABILITY_DATA`, two buffers in turn) with `prob_tables_offset` 0; (4) the RC process buffer starts with 15 words the driver writes (`src/av1enctmpl.h`); (5) the driver sets the loop filter level (7 at quantizer index 80 on key frames, 13 at 100 on P frames: libaom's pick-from-q rule, which we use) and the engine echoes it; CDEF on with two strengths (0, luma primary 4), damping from the status; loop restoration enabled in the sequence but NONE per plane; min CU 8x8; switchable interpolation filters and `reference_select` on P frames; tile control at 0x800 with inclusive corners copied into "next tile"; strip = whole frame (`stripID` 0, one strip, width / height in superblocks); tile statistics at 0x100 in the status. `enc.c` copies the traced 256x128 key / P setups (`scripts/av1enc-template.py` -> `src/av1enctmpl.h`) and patches the fields the traces at 256x128, 640x360 and 1080p showed to change (sizes, plane offsets, buffer sizes, strip / tile extent, timer, quantizer, loop filter level, quantizer per frame type). Earlier, headers-only findings: no colocated data (1), a 32-byte shift before the strip fields (the real cause: (1) above), codec numbers / ME controls / padding / tile flags made no difference |
| T12.03 | Rate control (CBR / VBR) | bitrate within 10 % of the target, every frame decodes | done: the driver's setup for `-rc cbr` / `-rc vbr` (traces `cbr`, `vbr`): MB-row modes in `SET_CONTROL_PARAMS` (18 CBR, 17 VBR), `delta_q_present` in the frame header (the engine varies the quantizer per block; our header signals it, `delta_q_res` 0), `nvenc_av1_rc_s` with HRD type 2, maxQPD 32, baseQPD 16, P/I and B/I ratios 294 / 330 (CBR) or 316 / 414 (VBR), frame rate and R / Ravg in 24.8 fixed point, the VBV size, Bmin = VBV / 81920 for CBR. The engine then picks each frame's base quantizer and loop filter level itself (status), which go into the header. 1080p, 120 frames: CBR 5 Mbit/s -> 5.26, VBR 8 (peak 12) -> 7.69; all frames decode (52-53 dB) |

| T12.05 | VideoToolbox `av01` encoder in libnvencvt | VTCompressionSession encodes AV1 with it; the samples decode | done (`vt/nvencvt.c`, `org.nvenc.videoencoder.av1`, "NVENC - AV1 - ...", rating 1100, no profile list; `NVENCVT_NO_AV1=1` leaves it out; `tools/vtencfile` writes what a VTCompressionSession emits): format description with an `av1C` atom (version 1, level, 4:2:0 / high bit depth, then our sequence header OBU), samples = temporal units without the temporal delimiter (ISOBMFF), sync / depends-on attachments as for H.264. 8-bit and 10-bit picked by the first frame's pixel format (420v / 420f / BGRA or x420 / xf20 / l10r are all offered, so VideoToolbox does not convert); Quality -> quantizer indices (the driver's 80 / 100 pair at the default), AverageBitRate -> CBR (MB-row). One reference (LAST). 1080p, 120 frames: 50 dB constant quantizer, 10-bit 50.6 dB (yuv420p10le), 6 Mbit/s real time -> 6.06; muxed to MP4 and decoded through VideoToolbox by our NVDEC AV1 decoder (M9): 120 of 120 frames bit-exact against dav1d, 441 fps. Open: more references, B frames, tiles / strips for 8K (the driver splits 4K into three EXECUTEs, trace `u3`, while one tile works for us up to 4K) |
| T12.06 | Tiles: frames wider than 4096 or larger than 4096x2304 (AV1 needs more than one tile; up to 8K) | 8K AV1 decodes, no drift | done 2026-10-20 (from the Linux driver's 8K trace `docs/traces/bframes-linux/a8k`): the uniform grid with the fewest tiles the spec allows (8K: 2x2; `ENC_AV1_TILE_ROWS_LOG2` for more rows), all in one strip on one engine: `num_tiles_minus1` / `num_strip_tiles_minus1` (0x148 / 0x144), `num_tile_cols` / `num_tile_rows` (0x160), one tile control per tile (corners, `tile_idx`, the next tile's corners, CDF update from tile 0), tile sizes from the status' tile statistics (16 bytes each at 0x100; the engine leaves 4 bytes before every tile for its size field). NVIDIA's driver splits 8K into two strips of 2x2 tiles, one per NVENC engine at once, with the filters off at the strip edge and an `NVENC_RC` (application 5) execute after each strip; one strip keeps every loop filter edge as the decoder applies it. Results: 1080p with 4 tiles, 4160x2160, 3840x2496 (2 tiles), 8K with 4 and 8 tiles all ~50.3 dB; 30 frames of 8K: no drift, 13.7 ms per frame (73 fps), our NVDEC AV1 decoder bit-exact on it (8.6 ms per frame); VideoToolbox `av01` 7680x4320 decodes (50.3 dB). Also checked: HEVC 7680x4320 (18.5 ms, 47.9 dB) and H.264 up to 8192x4320 (46.8 dB; level 6.0 above 36864 macroblocks now, was always 5.1) |
| T12.07 | Several references (AV1: LAST, LAST2, LAST3, GOLDEN) | content that comes back costs little; every frame decodes | done 2026-10-20 (Linux driver trace `ahq`, `-preset p7 -tune hq`: 4 references newest first in slots 1-4 rotating, the frame header's `ref_frame_idx` LAST..GOLDEN = newest..oldest): list 0 entry i = REF_PIC<i> (0x128 + i), temporal distance in half frames (0x12f + i), position i (0x136 + i), `num_ref_idx_l0_active` (0x144 bits 5-7), `unicompound_enable` (0x8d bit 2) from two references; the frame header gets each slot's order hint (skip mode becomes a coded flag with two forward references). `EncConfig.num_refs` up to 4 for AV1 (`ENC_MAX_REFS` 4; H.264 / HEVC stay at 3); libnvencvt's AV1 now uses 3 like the others (was 1). 1080p crowd_run at q 120/140: 1-4 references within 0.03 dB and 3 % in size, 1.13 -> 1.25 ms per frame; three pictures cycling: 1146 kbit/frame with one reference, 0.1 with three. dav1d and our NVDEC decoder (bit-exact) decode them. NVIDIA's p7 also turns on 4 luma CDEF strengths and luma loop restoration and spreads frames over both engines (not adopted) |
| T12.08 | B pictures (hidden ALTREF + `show_existing_frame`) | every frame decodes in display order | done 2026-10-20 (Linux driver traces `ab2s` / `ab2`, `-bf 2`): an anchor with B pictures before it in display order is coded with `show_frame` 0 (showable) and its frame OBU goes into the next B picture's temporal unit; after the last B picture a temporal unit with only a frame header OBU `show_existing_frame` shows it (`enc_av1_show_existing`). B pictures: list 0 = the anchors before (types LAST..), list 1 = ALTREF (type 6, REF_PIC6) = the anchor after, negative distance (0x12c / 0x133 / 0x13a, `num_ref_idx_l1_active` 0x145), `bicompound_enable` (0x8d bit 1), ALTREF sign bias (0x97), picture type B / not a reference (0x160), tile type B, quantizer P + 26 (the driver's 126 for 100), CDFs from ALTREF (`primary_ref_frame` 6), refresh none; NVIDIA's MD / ME control blocks for anchors and B pictures (setup 0x1b8..0x318, the same at 256x128 and 1080p; `src/av1enctmpl.h`). CDF tables are now kept per reconstruction slot (B pictures read the ALTREF's, anchors LAST's). `encodeN BFRAMES=n -av1`, libnvencvt `av01` when reordering is allowed and not real time (temporal units stay in presentation order: no decode time stamps; the anchor's sample is the show-existing unit after its B pictures). crowd_run 1080p at 12 Mbit/s CBR: 12.2 Mbit/s at 29.70 dB with 2 B pictures vs 13.9 Mbit/s at 29.89 dB P-only; 1.84 ms per frame. dav1d and our NVDEC decoder (bit-exact, `show_existing_frame` included) decode encodeN and VideoToolbox streams (key interval 0 and 25) |
| T12.09 | Quality mode (NVIDIA's default preset instead of low latency) | better PSNR at equal rate, decodes | done 2026-10-20: `EncConfig.quality` (libnvencvt: not real time) and B mode use the default preset's MD / ME control blocks (traces `ab2s`, same as p7 but for 5 bytes), its CDEF configuration (four luma strengths 0 / 2 / 4 / 9, `cdef_bits` 2) and luma self-guided loop restoration in 64x64 units (setup 0xa8..0xc8 except `base_q_idx`; frame header `lr_type` 3 / 0 / 0, `lr_unit_shift` 0; `av1_tmpl_hq_fh`). The engine picks the strengths / restoration per block and writes the coefficients. crowd_run 1080p: 8 Mbit/s CBR 28.36 -> 28.61 dB, constant q -2.4 % size and +0.21 dB; 1.1 -> 2.2 ms per frame. With 2 B pictures the rate/PSNR curve is another 0.2-0.4 dB higher (q sweep 90-150); VideoToolbox at 8 Mbit/s: not real time (B + quality) 28.44 dB vs real time 27.87 dB. dav1d and our decoder (bit-exact) decode all of it |

## M9: AV1 decode

Like VP9, the driver parses the headers and NVDEC decodes the tiles. Unlike VP9, the engine adapts the probabilities
itself (`AV1_SET_PROB_TAB_READ` / `_WRITE`, `context_update_tile_id`), so the driver only has to supply the default CDF
tables in the engine's layout and keep each reference frame's written table. That layout is the open question (not in
any public header). Hypothesis 1: libaom's `FRAME_CONTEXT` struct as it is (libaom is the AV1 reference codec, public,
BSD), with its inverted CDF values (32768 - x) and counters; dumped per quantizer context by a throwaway generator built
from libaom v3.12.1's entropy sources (`notes/av1/gen.c`, `notes/av1/aom_fc_q*.bin`, 21 240 bytes each; libaom is only
read, nothing from it is built into nvenc). Sources: AV1 specification (`vendor/specs/av1-spec.txt`), `nvdec_drv.h`,
`clc9b0.h`. Streams: `scripts/make-av1-streams.sh OUTDIR` (libaom, SVT-AV1, rav1e through ffmpeg; references from dav1d).

| Task | What | Done when | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| T9.00 | Default CDF tables from the spec text | every table's count matches its declared dimensions | done: `scripts/spec-tables.py av1` (constants read from the spec's own table, `a * b` products evaluated, page furniture stripped): 108 tables (94 CDF tables, 1196 CDF arrays) in `src/av1tables.h` |
| T9.01 | Parser: OBUs, sequence header, uncompressed frame header (frame refs incl. short signalling, superres, tile info, quantisation, segmentation, delta q / lf, loop filter, CDEF, loop restoration, tx / reference / skip mode, global motion, film grain), tile groups, reference slot state (7.20, 7.21) | the header fields match ffmpeg's `trace_headers` on every frame of every test stream | done (`src/av1parse.c`, `tools/av1parsetest`, `scripts/vp9-trace-compare.py` now also for AV1): 14 streams (libaom incl. alt-ref / show_existing_frame, 4x2 tiles, 10-bit, screen content, error resilient, film grain, 351x287; SVT-AV1 incl. 4K 10-bit, superres, film grain; rav1e incl. tiles), 0 differences in ~20 000 compared fields. Not covered by the streams yet: global motion, intra block copy |
| T9.02 | One key frame through `nvdec_av1_pic_s`: CDF table, tile info, filter buffers | bit-exact against dav1d | done (`src/av1dec.c`, `src/av1probs.c`, `tools/av1decodeN`): every frame of all 14 test streams bit-exact (libaom, SVT-AV1, rav1e: alt-ref / show_existing_frame, 4x2 tiles, 10-bit, 4K 10-bit at 3.2 ms/frame, screen content, error resilient, superres, film grain, 351x287). **Sources (user's decision 2026-10-19): headers-only probing first, then mesa-nova** (github.com/haiderking1/mesa-nova, branch `soka/nova`, NVK AV1 decode in Rust, MIT; by its own notes its findings come from NVIDIA's CUVID library) for what no header says. Headers-only findings: the application ID is `AVD` (0x12); scanning unknown IDs wedged the GPU once (never again); with the documented setup layout the engine accepted the job but returned status 0x10 without output; a null-address probe showed which buffers it reads. From mesa-nova: (1) tile entries are 16 bytes in the tile size buffer (`AV1TileInfo_OLD`: width / height in superblocks, start, end) - the tile stream info buffer is not used; (2) references LAST..ALTREF go in `SET_PICTURE_LUMA/CHROMA_OFFSET0..6`, the frame decoded in 8, `SET_PICTURE_INDEX` = frames decoded; (3) `show_frame` 1 always, error concealment and MB timer on, `gptimer_timeout_value` 10 000 cycles per macroblock (at least 8100); (4) the CDF table (0x2fc0 bytes): each table at a fixed offset and stride, values 32768 - x without the final 32768 and without counters; ours is built from the spec's tables (`av1probs.c`, byte-identical to mesa-nova's for all four quantizer contexts; the entries the spec does not define hold uniform CDFs); (5) global motion: per reference the six warp parameters (32-bit) and the shear (16-bit, 0x8000 when it cannot warp); (6) the motion field projections (libaom's choice) in `mf*_type` / `use_temporal*_mvs` / `mfmv_offset` / `mfmv_side` with the three column-MV read buffers; segment IDs read from the primary reference of the same size, else zeros, `prevsegid_flag`; (7) segmentation features encoded (alt-q magnitude + sign mask, REF_FRAME + 1 except on key frames, SKIP / GLOBALMV as 1); CDEF on only when it does something; superres steps 14 without superres; `lr_unit_size` 0x3f without loop restoration; the current frame's width is the coded width (before superres); (8) film grain: the driver gives the scaling functions and the grain templates (`AV1FilmGrainMemory`, spec 7.18.3) and a display picture (`SET_DISPLAY_BUF_*`), the decoder adds the grain; our addition: a hidden showable frame with grain gets its grained twin at decode time, output by its show_existing_frame |
| T9.03 | Inter frames: references, temporal MVs, segmentation maps, CDF save / load per slot, loop filter, CDEF, loop restoration, superres, film grain; libaom's test vectors | all test streams bit-exact | done: our 14 streams and every libaom test vector of 128x128 and up (`scripts/fetch-av1-vectors.sh`: allintra, intra-only + intra block copy with extreme DVs, CDF update, MVs, global motion, motion-field MVs, 3 SVC structures incl. 2 spatial layers, frame size up / down on inter frames, film grain 8 / 10-bit, 10-bit quantizers 0 / 31 / 63, monochrome 8 / 10-bit, 196x196, 202x210, 226x226) bit-exact on every frame. Refused (software decode instead): frames under 128x128 (NVIDIA's minimum: 16x16 to 34x34 came out grey with status 0xb, 66x66 decoded its key frame only), 4:2:2 / 4:4:4, 12-bit, more than 256 tiles. Monochrome: `chroma_format` 0, the engine writes 4:2:0 with neutral chroma. Lesson: a comment appended to a line of assignments swallowed `bit_depth` (every frame empty) and, unnoticed for a while, `disable_cdf_update` |
| T9.04 | VideoToolbox `av01` decoder in libnvencvt (av1C) | AVFoundation / ffmpeg `-hwaccel videotoolbox` decode AV1 with it | done (`vt/nvencvt_dec.c`, `org.nvenc.videodecoder.av1`, rating 1100; `NVENCVT_NO_AV1DEC=1` leaves it out): the process is opted in to AV1 like VP9; the session is sized for the largest frame of av1C's sequence header and fed that header first; NV12 / `x420`, monochrome as 4:2:0 with neutral chroma. Bit-exact against dav1d through VTDecompressionSession (1080p ~300 fps, 4K 10-bit, film grain, a size change mid-stream), AVAssetReader (1080p 399 fps, film grain 523 fps) and `ffmpeg -hwaccel videotoolbox` (31 of 34 streams / vectors identical, incl. film grain, SVC with 2 spatial layers, show_existing_frame, superres, 4K 10-bit, intra block copy). Found: (1) ffmpeg feeds hidden frames one by one and shows them itself on show_existing_frame: a hidden frame with film grain returns its grained twin; (2) a new sequence header announcing larger frames or another bit depth reallocates the session (it starts with a key frame); (3) a picture of a size other than the pool's gets a buffer made without the pool's Width / Height keys, and new pixel buffer attributes are set. Open (ffmpeg's side): `av1-1-b8-03-sizeup` / `-sizedown` through ffmpeg (it keeps its session across the new sequence header and its frames after the change are garbage; our buffers are bit-exact through VTDecompressionSession for the same stream); ffmpeg does not use VideoToolbox for monochrome AV1 |

## M10: VP9 decode

The driver parses both frame headers, keeps the four probability contexts, applies the compressed header's probability
updates and, after each frame, adapts the probabilities from the counts the engine wrote (backward adaptation); NVDEC
decodes the tiles. Source: VP9 Bitstream & Decoding Process Specification v0.7 (`vendor/specs/`, text via pdftotext),
`nvdec_drv.h`, `clc9b0.h`. Streams: `scripts/make-vp9-streams.sh OUTDIR` (libvpx through ffmpeg, with ffmpeg's reference
decodes).

| Task | What | Done when | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| T10.00 | Default probability tables from the spec text | every table's count matches its declared dimensions | done: `scripts/spec-tables.py vp9 vp9-spec.txt src/vp9tables.h` (strips page furniture and comments, joins wrapped declarations, checks counts; scan tables come out as uint16_t) |
| T10.01 | Parser: uncompressed header, compressed header (boolean decoder, `diff_update_prob`, `decode_term_subexp`, `inv_remap_prob`, MV updates), superframes (Annex B), `setup_past_independence`, `reset_frame_context`, the four saved contexts, refresh_probs + adaptation (8.4) from NVDEC's counter layout | the header fields match ffmpeg's `trace_headers` on every frame of every test stream; each compressed header ends exactly on its zero padding | done (`src/vp9parse.c`, `tools/vp9parsetest`, `scripts/vp9-trace-compare.py`): 11 streams (alt-ref with hidden frames and superframes, 1080p alt-ref, tiles, tile rows, error resilient, frame-parallel, lossless, segmentation, 4K, 10-bit profile 2, 351x287), 0 differences in 10 820 compared fields, every compressed header padding all-zero. The adaptation is untested until T10.03 (needs the engine's counts). Assumed, to check there: NVDEC's coefficient counts are [ZERO, ONE, TWO+, no-more] with `countEobs` = more_coefs reads, its inter-mode counts are the tree's branch counts (ZEROMV, NEARESTMV, NEARMV/NEWMV); `ref_frame_sign_bias` is cleared by `setup_past_independence` also for error-resilient inter frames (7.2, as written) |
| T10.02 | One key frame through `nvdec_vp9_pic_s`: probability table (`nvdec_vp9EntropyProbs_t`), segment, filter, tile-size and counter buffers | bit-exact against ffmpeg | done (`src/vp9dec.c`, `tools/vp9decodeN`): the first key frame was bit-exact once the engine had an intra top-line buffer, and the whole of 10 of the 11 test streams right after (the 11th is 10-bit, T10.03); see the T10.03 row. Found by experiment: (1) `SET_INTRA_TOP_BUF_OFFSET` (a generic method, not in the VP9 group) is required, else MMU fault at address 0 (Xid 31; bisected with a switch that pointed candidate methods at spare buffers); it gets ~4 bytes per pixel of width; (2) `mcomp_filter_type` takes the bitstream's literal filter order (smooth, regular, sharp, bilinear; 4 = switchable), not the spec's enum: frames with a fixed regular filter came out as smooth (42-68 dB) until mapped; (3) tile sizes: per tile in raster order, width and height in superblocks, 2 bytes each (`GIP_ASIC_TILE_SIZE`'s comment); (4) the bitstream buffer holds only the tile data (after both headers), `stream_len` its size; (5) the setup's surfaces: `SET_PICTURE_LUMA/CHROMA_OFFSET0..3` = LAST, GOLDEN, ALTREF, current (`VP9_FRAME_SFC_ID`), `SET_PICTURE_INDEX` 3; (6) column MVs: 1024 bytes per superblock, ping-pong (write current, read previous); segmentation maps: 32 bytes per superblock (`GIP_ASIC_VP9_CTB_SEG_SIZE`), ping-pong, swapped only when the map was updated; (7) filter buffer: deblocking top + left lines (`VP9_DBLK_TOP/LEFT_BUF_SIZE`), then `Vp9FltAboveOffset` (~57 bytes per row used at 4K), then `Vp9BsdCtrlOffset` (not written by these streams); (8) the assumed counter layouts (T10.01) are right: streams with backward adaptation are bit-exact |
| T10.03 | Inter frames: reference slots, sign bias / compound, column MVs (previous frame), segmentation map read/write, backward adaptation from the counters, hidden frames, show_existing_frame, intra-only frames, resolution changes / scaled references, 10/12-bit | all test streams bit-exact | done: bit-exact on every frame of our 10 libvpx streams and 27 of libvpx's public test vectors (`scripts/fetch-vp9-vectors.sh`): show_existing_frame (3 vectors), intra-only start, inter-frame resizing (scaled references, 3), key-frame resizing (2), tiles 4x4 / 4x1 / 16-8 with resizing, sizes 8x8, 66x66, 130x132, 226x226, 351x287, delta-q, loop filter deltas, segmentation (segkey, adaptive quantisation), skip, frame-parallel, big superframes, 3-layer SVC. Refused: `largescaling` (19200x108, beyond NVDEC's 8192; the engine answers status 0x10) and 4:4:4 (profile 1; not an NVDEC VP9 format). Found: (1) the engine does not clamp reference reads at the frame edge but reads up to the superblock-aligned size, so the driver repeats the last column / row into that padding of every reference (`extend_edges`; 8x8 and 66x66 were wrong without it; extending to the 64-aligned size is enough even with a larger pitch); (2) a stream may start with intra-only frames (8.2); (3) reference decodes must keep every frame (`-fps_mode passthrough`): ffmpeg's raw video output otherwise duplicates / drops frames around hidden and show_existing frames, which looked like decoder errors. (4) 10/12-bit: `v1.bit_depth` = the bit depth; the engine writes 16-bit samples MSB-aligned (like P010) in the same tiled layout with a byte pitch twice as wide, but `framestride` and the reference strides count samples, not bytes (with bytes, 10-bit rows landed twice as far apart). Bit-exact: libvpx's 10-bit vector and our 10-bit 1280x720, 1366x768, 3840x2160 (3.0 ms/frame) and 12-bit 640x360 |
| T10.04 | VideoToolbox `vp09` decoder in `libnvencvt` (vpcC), 10-bit output | AVFoundation / ffmpeg `-hwaccel videotoolbox` decode VP9 with it | done (`vt/nvencvt_dec.c`, `org.nvenc.videodecoder.vp9`, rating 1100; `tools/vtdecode` gained `VTDECODE_REF` / `VTDECODE_PF` / `VTDECODE_AVREAD` / `VTDECODE_SUPP`): NV12 for 8-bit, `x420` (the engine's MSB-aligned 16-bit samples as they are) for 10-bit, 12-bit refused (no CoreVideo 12-bit 4:2:0 biplanar format). Bit-exact against ffmpeg's software decode through VTDecompressionSession (1080p 400 fps, 4K 120 fps, 10-bit 720p 330 fps), AVAssetReader (alwaysCopiesSampleData NO: 1080p 394, 4K 110 fps) and `ffmpeg -hwaccel videotoolbox` (identical output on 12 of 13 streams tried, incl. show_existing_frame, intra-only, 10-bit, SVC and inter-frame resizing). Found: (1) VideoToolbox offers VP9 decoders only to processes that opt in (`VTRegisterSupplementalVideoDecoderIfAvailable`, public since macOS 11; WebKit and ffmpeg call it); Apple's own VP9 decoder is not available on this system at all, so the library opts the process in when it registers (`NVENCVT_NO_VP9SUPP=1` leaves it to the app); (2) ffmpeg splits superframes and feeds hidden frames one by one, expecting a picture for each (it shows them itself on show_existing_frame): a sample that shows nothing emits the frame it decoded (reporting it dropped made ffmpeg tear the session down); (3) ffmpeg re-creates the session whenever the frame size changes (inter-frame resizing, spatial SVC), so the next frame needs references the old session had: a VP9 decoder is parked for 3 s when its session ends and the next session of the same bit depth takes it over (`vp9dec_migrate` copies the references into a larger one). Open: after re-creating its session at an odd size (vp90-2-18-resize, 155x115) ffmpeg's frames lose the last chroma row / column; our buffers are bit-exact through VTDecompressionSession for that stream (one session, buffers of each frame's size), and a stream that is 155x115 from the start is exact through ffmpeg too |
